slides.title: The Case for Managing Data
slides.intro: Deriving value from data does not happen by accident — it requires management and leadership.

columns.heading: What Data Represents
bullets: A vital enterprise asset enabling insight into customers, products, and services
Called the 'currency', 'life blood', and 'new oil' of the information economy
Essential to day-to-day operations — organisations cannot transact without data
A means to innovate and reach strategic goals

columns.heading: What Management Requires
bullets: Intention, planning, coordination, and commitment — value does not happen by accident
Shared responsibility between business and IT roles
Collaboration to ensure high-quality data that meets strategic needs

columns.heading: Data Management
columns.body: Data Management is the development, execution, and supervision of plans, policies, programs, and practices that deliver, control, protect, and enhance the value of data and information assets throughout their lifecycles.

columns.heading: Data Management Professional
columns.body: A Data Management Professional is any person who works in any facet of data management (from technical management of data throughout its lifecycle to ensuring that data is properly utilized and leveraged) to meet strategic organizational goals.

left.heading: Effective Data Management
points: Enables organisations to get value from their data assets
Delivers reliable, high-quality data for better decisions
Provides competitive advantage through information and knowledge
Mirrors the management of financial and physical assets

right.heading: Failure to Manage Data
points: Similar to failure to manage capital
Results in waste and lost opportunity
Leaves the potential value of data assets untapped
Prevents organisations from reaching strategic goals
